### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handlePackagesRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `230f6e1766012c832e95c0c3267e2619e4aa0495` — the merge of head `af581fe0716949730f1743ff14e74cbfb3b45bd6` into base `35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 230f6e1766012c832e95c0c3267e2619e4aa0495 && git checkout 230f6e1766012c832e95c0c3267e2619e4aa0495
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01 af581fe0716949730f1743ff14e74cbfb3b45bd6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01 && git merge --no-ff af581fe0716949730f1743ff14e74cbfb3b45bd6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `af581fe0716949730f1743ff14e74cbfb3b45bd6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-publish-drafts-request-conformance.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-publish-drafts-change-note.integration.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`error()`), packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`readPublishBackfillRequest`, `publishBackfillRefusal`), packages/client/src/index.ts (`packages.publishDrafts`), ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts (`publishPackageDrafts`), .changeset/28406-publish-drafts-request-schema.md, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs

Faces: two faces made this review owed and one record covers both. `reviewFace` over the PR's file list returns `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` as its `hits` (the schema face: a published-schema source file, docblock only), and the PR body and changeset both open a line `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (the narrowing face), whose floor is every diff path outside the prose faces; the changeset is the one prose-face path, read for ② below. PR #28527, one commit on `claude/project-thread-x4768u` over merge base `1f1a369b5`, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, six files, +99/−17. Read against card #28452, its triage `6547072197` and unblock `6547725928`, merged PR #28447, the dispatch order, the dev report `6553617357` and the seat's claim amendment `6553627544`. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally; the recogniser template was printed from `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template`, which reads no board.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set change at `POST /packages/:id/publish-drafts`, derived from the one code hunk in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` (the `publish-drafts` branch):

1. **What moves from accept to refuse: exactly the bodies that are an object whose `message` key is present and not a string.** The door now calls `PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema.shape.message.safeParse(body?.message)`; the member on `main` is `z.string().optional()`, so `undefined` passes with `data: undefined` and every other non-string fails. A number, an object, an array and `null` move from `200` (published, default note) to `400`. `null` moves, because `.optional()` admits only `undefined` under zod 4; the conformance suite pins `{ message: null }` refused. Judged correct and matches the triage ruling ("refuse 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming message").
2. **What does not move.** The empty string stays accepted (it is a string; the conformance suite's accepted-bodies case still carries `{ message: '', backfill: [] }` and the schema's `describe` text, "Absent or empty, those rows record the sentence naming the package", still holds). An absent `message`, an absent body, a `null` body, and a body that is not an object all read `body?.message` as `undefined` and publish with the default note as before. No other declared key narrows: `backfill` is deliberately not parsed at the door and is still forwarded as sent. Judged correct. Residual, recorded under ③ rather than as a must-fix: a whole-body `[]`, string or number is a body the schema would refuse that the door still answers `200` on; the ruling named `message`, the PR body states this residual truthfully ("A body that is not an object (or absent) has no `message` and publishes with the default note, as before"), and it is not this card's defect.
3. **Unknown keys still stripped; `actor` still answers 200.** The door reads no other body key than `message` and `backfill`, so a body `actor` is never looked at; the conformance suite keeps the `{ actor: 'someone_else', message: 'note' }` 200 pin and the ADR-0045 re-save pin, and adds `{ actor: 'x', message: 7 }` to the refusal set (refused for `message`, not for `actor`). `@objectstack/client`'s `packages.publishDrafts` still sends `opts` whole, deprecated `actor` included, and still works. Judged correct.
4. **One refusal for a bad `backfill`, same answer as base.** The door forwards `body.backfill` unchanged to `protocol.publishPackageDrafts`, where `readPublishBackfillRequest` throws `publishBackfillRefusal` (status 400, code `VALIDATION_ERROR`, headline plus `issues[]`), exactly as on `main`; the door's `catch` path for that throw is untouched by this diff. The real-protocol conformance case (five malformed shapes, `publish` called once, response names the entry path) is unchanged and still pins it. Had the door parsed the whole body, a bad `backfill` would have met two judges with two sentences; the member parse keeps one. Judged correct and the right reading of the order's "measure whether parsing at the door would double-judge it".
5. **Refusal envelope matches the sibling doors; no second envelope.** The new leg answers `deps.error(text, 400)` with no explicit code, exactly as the install door's `manifest.id`, `manifest.version` and whole-body legs do a few hundred lines above; `HttpDispatcher.error()` hands it to `apiErrorResponse`, which derives `VALIDATION_ERROR` from the 400 through the standard catalog (`standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus`), so nothing in `packages/spec` moves and no code is minted. The text names the member (`message: Invalid input: expected string, received …`) and carries the prescription without a tracker number. Order: after the `403`/walled/query-parameter/`501`/`404` legs and before the publish, beside the protocol's `backfill` judgement, the same position relative to its id gate that the install door's body legs occupy. Judged correct.
6. **Pins and prose flipped.** The known-divergence case in `packages-publish-drafts-request-conformance.test.ts` ("dropped by the door, not refused") is replaced by the refusal case (five bodies: status, code, headline matches `message:`, `publishPackageDrafts` and `saveMetaItem` never called), and its header bullet for `message` and the "does not claim the door parses the body" sentence are rewritten to the new truth. `route-ledger.ts`: the publish-drafts row's `note` now says `message` is parsed with the schema's member and a non-string is refused 400; `requestSchema`/`responseSchema` and every other field of the row unchanged, so the client's ledger resolver test is unaffected. `packages-publish-drafts-change-note.integration.test.ts` (real door, real protocol, ObjectQL, on-disk SQLite) adds the end-to-end case: `42`, `{}`, `[]` each refused, no `publish` history row and no `sys_metadata_commit` row afterwards, then the same draft publishes with a string note and the row carries it. Judged correct.
7. **The spec docblock is now true.** On `main` the `PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema` docblock reads "`message` — forwarded only when it is a string", which this diff makes false; the head says the note is parsed with the declaration's member and a refused one answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `message`. The sentence before it ("The door reads exactly two body members and hands them to `publishPackageDrafts`") remains true. JSDoc only: no `describe`, key, type or export moves, so `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` (built from `describe` text, which is unchanged), `api-surface`, `authorable-surface`, `json-schema.manifest` and `declaration-map` do not move; none of them is in the diff and none needs to be. Judged correct.
8. **Public surface.** No export added, removed or renamed in `@objectstack/spec`; no SDK signature changes in `@objectstack/client`; the `.d.ts` bytes of `@objectstack/spec` change only by the docblock text, which is why the `@objectstack/spec` patch line is right (② below).
9. **First-party callers.** `packages/client/src/index.ts` `packages.publishDrafts` types `message?: string` and serialises `opts` as given; `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts` `publishPackageDrafts` sends `message` only when `options.message !== undefined`, with its options type picked from the SDK's (`message?: string`). Every `ui/` call site reached through that method (`StudioDesignSurface`, `PackagesPage`, `usePublishAllDrafts`, `PendingDraftsBar`, `AiChatPage`, `DraftChangesPanel`) is typed through it; no call site constructs a non-string note. `packages/cli`, `skills/**` and `content/docs/**` contain no caller of this door. No first-party caller breaks.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the correct declaration**, not the order's expected `yes (narrowing)`. `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines the four combinations: `yes (narrowing)` is "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read"; `no (narrowing)` is "NOT a widening, but breaking. This is the whole point of the arm." This diff widens nothing: no key, value or export is added and no body previously refused is now accepted. The dev's departure from the order is right and the seat's amendment `6553627544` adopts it. Same line, same spelling, in the PR body and the changeset, with the arm closed before the em-dash reasoning, so the reader takes the arm.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`** is correct: nothing an author writes in metadata changes; the narrowing is on a REST request body, not on a metadata type. Under `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s level axis, `none` must grade every introduced entry `patch` and may move no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` baseline: both entries are `patch` and no `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` shard is in the diff (the schema's keys and `describe` text are unchanged, so none should be). Consistent.
- **Levels.** `@objectstack/runtime: patch` and `@objectstack/spec: patch`. Per the Post-Task Checklist, "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"; the changeset carries `fix(runtime)!:`, the `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing` banner and exactly one marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. That category is refused only when the body carries a FROM → TO migration prescription; this body carries none (the one-line "send it as a string, or leave it out" is the refusal's own prescription to a caller, not a consumer-code rewrite block), and nothing was ever stored for a refused body, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite. Judged consistent with the gate. `check-empty-changeset.mjs`: the frontmatter is non-empty and the diff adds its own changeset without touching the pending `28406-publish-drafts-request-schema.md` (a foreign changeset it may not edit); the body instead states that it supersedes that changeset's "Nothing changes on the wire" sentence, which is the right way to do it.
- **Two-sided effect on the declared contract.** The pending `@objectstack/spec` minor for `PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema` promised the door reads the body as before; this patch retracts that promise at the door. Both ship in the same release train, so the release-notes compiler sees both sentences; the superseding sentence in this changeset is what makes that readable.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev-raised departure 1, Clause-② arm.** Answered under ②: `no (narrowing)` is right; the order's `yes (narrowing)` would have declared a widening that does not exist. No escalation.
- **Dev-raised departure 2, file surface.** `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (docblock) and the `@objectstack/spec` patch line were outside the claim's file surface; the seat amended the claim in `6553627544`, so the committed tree and the claim now agree. No governed path is in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success` on this head). Closed.
- **`open_questions`: []**, **`out_of_scope_findings`: none** in the report. Accepted; one reviewer observation below.
- **Reviewer observation, not a must-fix.** A whole body that is not an object (a JSON array, string or number) is a body the schema refuses that the door still answers `200` on with the default note, because `body?.message` reads `undefined`. The ruling scoped this card to `message`, and the PR body states the residual plainly. It is a declared-not-enforced remainder on the same door; the seat should file it as its own finding (Prime Directive 10) rather than widen this PR.
- **Evidence read in the dev report.** Red-first: the two new cases run against the base door, both red on `{"message":42}: expected 200 to be 400`, eleven controls green. Green at the fix: 13/13 across the two files. Ablation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the anchor `if (!declaredMessage.success) {`, which restores the string-only forward (a failed parse carries no `data`, so the spread sends no note): anchor 1 → 0, blob changed, both refusal cases red, eleven controls green (string note, no body, `actor` stripped, undeclared members, real-protocol `backfill` refusal), restore blob equals head and `git diff HEAD` empty; the runtime tests import the door from `src/`, so no build stands between the mutation and the run. Runtime typecheck exit 0; runtime suite 498 files, 8085 passed, 19 skipped; dogfood battery 363 files, 2932 passed, 28 skipped, no failure; 84 derived gate families run and reconciled with `--ran`. The evidence is specific to the mechanism (the ablation restores the exact prior behaviour and only the two refusal cases turn red), so it is accepted as proving the fix rather than the test harness.
- **Head check-runs at this read.** Completed `success`: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Spec property liveness`, the scoped lint lanes and the docs guards. Still `in_progress`: `Build Core`, `Test Core` (8 shards), the four `Type Check` lanes (which carry `check:docs`, `check:api-surface` and the other spec artifact gates), the `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` lanes, `Build UI Deps`, `Live E2E UI`. This record is the contract-tier verdict; the landing pre-check that every check is green on this head is the seat's, read before the PR enters the queue, and no red is expected from a diff of this shape (no spec `describe`, export or authorable key moves).
- **Docs drift check** names `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` through `handlePackagesRequest`; that page describes the walled-catalog refusal at the `/packages` write doors, which still precedes the new leg, so the page stays accurate.
- **Author.** `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no off-relay author note is owed. The commit carries the model-free `Claude-Session` and `Co-authored-by` trailer pair; no model identifier appears in the PR title, body, changeset, or code comments.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Narrowing face, against the published spec on `main`.** The narrowing takes no declared capability away at the consumer: `PublishPackageDraftsRequestSchema` on `main` already declares `message?: string`, so a caller that honoured the published declaration never sent a non-string note, and the SDK and `MetadataClient` types never allowed one. What the diff does is make the spec's own refusal real at the door, which is Prime Directive 12 (reject off-spec input at the producer-facing door, never tolerate it in the consumer) and the North Star's "错的必须被响亮拒绝并给处方" line the triage cited; the previous behaviour (silently dropping the note and publishing) was the declared-not-enforced shape Prime Directive 10 forbids. The chosen mechanism, parsing the declaration's member by reference rather than restating the rule, is the same move the install door already makes with `ManifestSchema.shape.id` and `.shape.version`, so the file's two body-validating doors now follow one pattern. Judged to hold.
- **Why the member parse and not the whole-body parse the triage's words suggest.** The dev measured the alternative: a whole-body `safeParse` would refuse a malformed `backfill` at the door with a second sentence and no `issues[]`, displacing the protocol's one refusal that the SDK, Studio and the `backfill` conformance suite already read. Keeping the protocol as the single judge of `backfill`, and parsing only the member whose enforcement was missing, satisfies both halves of the order ("exactly one refusal for a bad backfill, with the same answer as today") and leaves the whole-body remainder named under ③. Judged the correct trade; the alternative of parsing the whole body and filtering `backfill` issues would have been a second dialect of the same judgement.
- **Schema face, `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`.** A docblock-only change that brings the declaration's prose into line with its first consumer, the door; the `describe` text (what the generated reference prints) was already correct and does not move. The hunk makes no claim the cited code does not now bear out. Judged to hold.
- **Scenario the card is accepted against.** `{"message": 42}` through the real door: base `200` with the default note; head `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `message`, nothing published, no history row, and the draft still pending so a corrected request publishes it with its note. Pinned at two layers (dispatcher over a protocol double; real protocol over on-disk SQLite). Controls for every "unchanged" claim in the PR body are pinned in the same suites. The acceptance scenario holds.
- No must-fix found on any face.
